etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old English ane (“(for) a”) hwile (“while”).

definitions.definition: For some time; for a short time.

quote.citation: c. 1596–97, William Shakespeare, The Merchant of Venice‎[1], act 1, scene 1:
quote.text: Gratiano: […] Fare ye well awhile:I'll end my exhortation after dinner.

quote.citation: 1944 May and June, “When the Circle was Steam Operated”, in Railway Magazine, page 137:
quote.text: Engine No. 18 went off into a shed to rest awhile, and No. 7, a precisely similar one, backed on to the train in her place.

quote.citation: 1979, The Boomtown Rats (lyrics and music), “Wind Chill Factor (Minus Zero)”, in The Fine Art of Surfacing:
quote.text: I'll slip beneath these sheets and shiver here awhile / I find this happening more frequently these days

definitions.definition: (US, Pennsylvania Dutch English) In the meantime; during an implicit ongoing process.
